title: GET /api/v1/quote accepts invalid slippage and amountIn: NaN tolerance silently corrupts quote output (minAmountOut serialized as null)
reasoning: In the GET /quote handler, slippage is computed as Number.parseFloat(c.req.query("slippage") ?? "0.5") / 100 with no regex, finite, or range validation (contrast v3-quote.ts lines 23/35 which enforce 0-5). A non-numeric value such as "abc" yields NaN, which propagates into swapService.getQuote as slippageTolerance; any derived numeric field then serializes as null in the 200 response (JSON.stringify(NaN) → null), silently corrupting minAmountOut/price impact instead of returning 400. amountIn is likewise only presence-checked (line 145), so non-numeric input surfaces as a service-level 500 with String(err) instead of a 400. The companion /build and /record handlers are not affected, but this endpoint has no tests at all.
reproduction: GET /api/v1/quote?tokenIn=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001&tokenOut=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000002&amountIn=1000000000000000000&slippage=abc returns HTTP 200 with minAmountOut: null instead of 400.
recommendation: Validate slippage with a bounded finite check (e.g., 0 <= slippage <= 5, mirroring v3-quote.ts) and validate amountIn against /^\d+$/ before calling getQuote; return 400 for violations. Add handler-level tests covering non-numeric and out-of-range params.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only included test file (apps/api/test/price-guard.test.ts) covers the pure evaluatePriceGuard function; no test exercises the swap route handlers or their query-param validation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Assert GET /quote with slippage=abc and with amountIn=abc both return 400, and that a valid request never returns null for minAmountOut.
